behavior: Usually seen in pairs or small groups. Forages mainly on the ground but also in trees, taking insects and other arthropods, small vertebrates, seeds, fruit, and nectar. Often flicks the tail sharply upward. Both sexes sing and frequently perform musical duets.
field_marks: Entirely black plumage with a subtle blue-violet sheen
Sharply pointed, slightly curved black bill
Dark brown eye without a contrasting eye-ring
Large black legs and strong feet
Plain black wings without bars or patches
habitat: Semi-open to open tropical and lower-subtropical landscapes, including forest edges and clearings, open woodland, plantations, pastures, parks, and gardens with scattered trees; generally avoids dense forest and thick undergrowth.

measurements.wingspan: Not reported; no cm range available in the consulted species accounts
